views.name: dogs_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  dog_id,
  owner_id,
  abandoned_yn,
  breed_code,
  size_code,
  name,
  age,
  date_of_birth,
  gender,
  CASE WHEN trim(weight) = '' THEN NULL ELSE CAST(weight AS REAL) END AS weight,
  date_arrived,
  date_adopted,
  date_departed
FROM Dogs
views.description: Canonicalized dog-level projection. Use as the cleaned base for dog-centric queries (preserves identifiers and key timestamps, casts numeric-like text to numeric where reasonable). | Use for: List dogs with numeric weight available; Filter dogs by arrival/adoption/departure dates; Join dogs to owners/breeds/sizes or treatments

views.name: owners_contact
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  owner_id,
  first_name,
  last_name,
  street,
  city,
  state,
  zip_code,
  email_address,
  home_phone,
  cell_number
FROM Owners
views.description: Owner contact projection; keeps identifying and contact fields for joins and contact lists. | Use for: Retrieve owner contact details for notifications; Join owner info to dogs for mailing lists or owner-dog summaries

views.name: treatments_fact
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  treatment_id,
  dog_id,
  professional_id,
  treatment_type_code,
  date_of_treatment,
  CASE WHEN cost_of_treatment IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(cost_of_treatment AS REAL) END AS cost_of_treatment
FROM Treatments
views.description: Event-level treatments projection exposing core event attributes and numeric cost for financial analysis or joins to dogs/professionals. | Use for: Compute treatment counts or costs per dog/professional; Filter treatments by date ranges or type

views.name: dogs_with_dim
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dog_id,
  d.owner_id,
  d.abandoned_yn,
  d.breed_code,
  b.breed_name,
  d.size_code,
  s.size_description,
  d.name,
  d.age,
  d.date_of_birth,
  d.gender,
  d.weight,
  d.date_arrived,
  d.date_adopted,
  d.date_departed,
  o.first_name AS first_name,
  o.last_name AS last_name,
  o.email_address AS email_address,
  o.city AS city,
  o.state AS state
FROM Dogs d
LEFT JOIN Breeds b ON d.breed_code = b.breed_code
LEFT JOIN Sizes s ON d.size_code = s.size_code
LEFT JOIN Owners o ON d.owner_id = o.owner_id
views.description: Denormalized dog rows joined to descriptive breed and size labels and owner contact info. Use for display tables and cohort selection that needs metadata about each dog. | Use for: Create dog listings with owner and breed/size metadata; Filter dogs by owner city/state, breed, or size

views.name: treatments_enriched
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.treatment_id,
  t.dog_id,
  d.name AS name,
  d.breed_code,
  b.breed_name,
  t.professional_id,
  p.first_name AS prof_first_name,
  p.last_name AS prof_last_name,
  t.treatment_type_code,
  tt.treatment_type_description,
  t.date_of_treatment,
  t.cost_of_treatment
FROM Treatments t
LEFT JOIN Dogs d ON t.dog_id = d.dog_id
LEFT JOIN Breeds b ON d.breed_code = b.breed_code
LEFT JOIN Professionals p ON t.professional_id = p.professional_id
LEFT JOIN Treatment_Types tt ON t.treatment_type_code = tt.treatment_type_code
views.description: Treatments events enriched with dog attributes, treatment type description, and professional name for event-level reporting. | Use for: Event-level reports of treatments with dog and professional context; Aggregate treatment costs by breed or professional

views.name: treatment_counts_per_dog
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  dog_id,
  COUNT(*) AS treatment_count,
  SUM(cost_of_treatment) AS total_treatment_cost,
  MIN(date_of_treatment) AS first_treatment_date,
  MAX(date_of_treatment) AS last_treatment_date
FROM Treatments
GROUP BY dog_id
views.description: Aggregated counts and total cost of treatments per dog. Useful as a dog-level measure table to join back to dogs for summaries or thresholds. | Use for: Find dogs with most treatments or highest treatment cost; Filter dogs by having zero/one/more treatments; Identify recent or old treatment activity per dog

views.name: treatment_counts_per_professional
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  professional_id,
  COUNT(*) AS treatment_count,
  SUM(cost_of_treatment) AS total_treatment_cost,
  MIN(date_of_treatment) AS first_treatment_date,
  MAX(date_of_treatment) AS last_treatment_date
FROM Treatments
GROUP BY professional_id
views.description: Aggregates treatments by professional: counts and total cost. Use for workload and revenue summaries per professional. | Use for: Which professionals performed the most treatments or generated most cost; Workload distribution across professionals

views.name: latest_treatment_per_dog
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.treatment_id,
  t.dog_id,
  t.professional_id,
  t.treatment_type_code,
  t.date_of_treatment,
  t.cost_of_treatment,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t.dog_id ORDER BY t.date_of_treatment DESC, t.treatment_id DESC) AS treatment_rank
FROM Treatments t
views.description: Latest treatment event per dog (one row per dog) exposing a rank so downstream queries can select top N or the single latest treatment. Use to find last activity for each dog. | Use for: Get latest treatment per dog (WHERE treatment_rank = 1); Find recent inactive dogs by comparing last treatment date to thresholds

views.name: running_costs_by_dog
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.treatment_id,
  t.dog_id,
  t.date_of_treatment,
  t.cost_of_treatment,
  SUM(COALESCE(t.cost_of_treatment,0)) OVER (PARTITION BY t.dog_id ORDER BY t.date_of_treatment ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_total_cost
FROM Treatments t
views.description: Per-dog running total of treatment costs ordered by treatment date. Useful to observe cost accumulation over time per dog and to select temporal thresholds. | Use for: Plot cumulative treatment cost per dog over time; Find the point when a dog's cumulative cost exceeded a threshold

views.name: breed_size_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  breed_code,
  size_code,
  COUNT(dog_id) AS dog_count
FROM Dogs d
GROUP BY breed_code, size_code
views.description: Counts of dogs by breed and size (one row per breed_code and size_code pair). Useful as a pivot input for population mixes or dashboards. | Use for: Distribution of dogs across breeds and sizes; Pivot into wide form by breed or size in downstream queries
